title: Structure of the space of folding protein sequences defined by large language models.
summary: The paper uses ESMFold-predicted structures to define an effective foldability energy, then statistical-mechanics sampling to find that natural protein-G sequences occupy a wider low-energy basin than sampled artificial sequences. This is a model-dependent computational result for the studied protein, not experimental confirmation or a general result for all proteins. The study does not establish external generalization, causal effects or sustained operational impact.
